state.case_summary:
A man in his 70s with a history of coronary artery bypass surgery, ejection fraction of 25% and biventricular pacemaker placement was brought to the emergency department for dull chest pain of 2 hours' duration.

No detailed physical examination findings were provided in the case report.

- ECG findings:    Image 1 Title: First Electrocardiogram From Patient's Current Presentation    Image Description: Shows sinus activity at 72 beats/min, normal PR interval, QRS duration of 160 milliseconds. Ventricular depolarization preceded by 2 pacing stimuli occurring less than 40 milliseconds apart. ST segment depression >1mm in V2 and V3, new discordant ST elevation of 1mm in leads II, III, and aVF, with new reciprocal ST depression <1mm in aVL.    Image 2 Title: Patient's Electrocardiogram From 3 Years Before    Image Description: Baseline ECG after biventricular pacemaker placement    Image 3 Title: Magnified and Isolated Reading From Lead V5    Image Description: Shows two ventricular pacing spikes with an offset of less than 40 milliseconds    Image 4 Title: Patient's Electrocardiogram After Catheterization    Image Description: Shows resolution of ST segment changes  - Laboratory Tests:    - Initial troponin (2 hours after symptom onset): Negative  - Cardiac Catheterization:    Revealed thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft proximal to circumflex anastomosis and occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery

root.label: Acute Chest Pain Syndrome with Suspected Ischaemic Aetiology and New Discordant ST Elevation

Thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft
Occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery
